tasks.short: Consult buying personnel about expected product and service demand.

steps.what: Review category sales, stock movements and existing demand forecasts.
Request buying personnel's category observations before the discussion.
Discuss demand signals, supplier intelligence and disagreements with buying personnel.
Write a demand insight brief separating observations, hypotheses and unresolved questions.

loop.input: Discussion notes and category trading snapshot with source references.
loop.output: Demand insight brief with attributed observations, hypotheses and open questions.
loop.check: Link factual statements to sources; verify numbers mechanically; manager checks interpretation and omitted disagreements.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; unresolved claims stay flagged for manual editing.
loop.why_not_simpler: A template structures the brief, but free-text observations need concise synthesis.

steps.what: Select demand hypotheses for research and approve follow-up owners.
Send agreed actions and deadlines to buying personnel and research colleagues.

tasks.design: Configure a category view in the {ERP} and recurring advice requests through the {WORKFLOW}. A bounded drafting loop turns written discussion notes into a source-linked brief in the {DOCS}; the manager approves research actions in the {PROJECT}, which triggers notifications through the {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Category data and buyer observations arrive separately. Software can collect figures, but informal advice needs interpretation.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing reporting and notification features handle the structured work. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of connecting records and adding a bounded drafting step.
tasks.still_hard: Buyers may disagree, hold tacit knowledge or repeat supplier optimism. A polished brief cannot establish whether demand will materialise.
tasks.human_edge: Probe weak signals, understand commercial incentives and distinguish confident opinions from evidence.

ambition.what: Weekly selection of a category demand hypothesis to test.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time assembling briefs and chasing actions, leaving more time to challenge demand assumptions. Formal research and spending authority stays unchanged.

reach.task: Turn buyer demand hypotheses into small research tests.
reach.learn: Sampling, question design and the difference between stated interest and purchasing behaviour.

evidence.claim: Structured reporting and notifications can support buyer consultation; interpretation and relationship work remain human.
Coosto provides listening dashboards and trend alerts, demonstrating an optional source of demand signals, not automated buyer consultation.
Time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured results.

assumptions: Category sales and stock records are available in the {ERP}.
Routine requests use agreed questions and a maintained internal recipient list.
Written discussion notes are available; recording and transcription are outside scope.
Access timing includes GDPR checks and employee consultation under national rules where applicable.
unknowns: Which category data the manager can access and how fresh it is.
Whether buyer advice currently arrives mainly in meetings or written messages.
Who can assign research work and approve its budget.
Which employee consultation requirements apply under national rules.
research_questions: Can existing reporting configuration produce a useful category snapshot without a custom connector?
Does the drafting loop preserve disagreements and uncertainty in representative discussion notes?
new_work: Review draft briefs for attribution, uncertainty and missing objections.
Maintain category mappings, recipient lists and recurring questions.
Resolve stale data and failed notifications.

tasks.short: Negotiate distribution agreements with vendors or distributors.

steps.what: Review distribution volumes, service performance, costs and margins.
Request proposals from selected vendors or distributors.
Compare proposal prices, coverage, service commitments and commercial exceptions.

loop.input: Supplier proposals and a fixed commercial comparison schema.
loop.output: Source-linked proposal fields, exclusions and missing terms.
loop.check: Require page references; validate currencies, units and dates; calculate scenarios deterministically; reviewer checks material terms.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass per proposal; ambiguous terms go to procurement.
loop.why_not_simpler: Calculations are deterministic, but proposals describe coverage and exceptions in inconsistent free text.

steps.what: Agree negotiation limits, preferred coverage and acceptable commercial trade-offs.
Negotiate coverage, pricing, incentives and service commitments within the approved mandate.
Prepare the agreement using agreed terms and the approved contract template.
Review legal departures and approve the agreement for signature.
Sign the approved agreement and obtain the counterparty's signature.

tasks.design: Combine reporting from the {ERP} and {OPS_SYSTEM} with a proposal comparison generator that extracts source-linked terms and calculates scenarios deterministically. Populate approved templates in the {DOCS}, route legal and commercial approvals through the {WORKFLOW}, and release the approved version to the {ESIGN} after signatory approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Comparable costs require manual normalisation, while proposal exceptions sit in documents and email threads. Negotiation itself depends on bargaining power and trust.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding makes comparison tools and approval connections cheaper to build. Bounded extraction can structure proposals without giving software negotiating authority.
tasks.still_hard: Exclusivity, territorial rights, service risk and concessions need commercial and legal judgement. Missing operational data can make precise comparisons misleading.
tasks.human_edge: Read the counterparty's priorities, trade concessions and protect the long-term distribution relationship.
tasks.altitude: The manager spends less preparation time reconciling proposals and more time testing distribution options with operations and finance. Negotiation and signature limits stay unchanged.

reach.task: Assess market coverage gaps before distributor negotiations.
reach.learn: Territory analysis, channel overlap and evidence of unmet customer demand.

reach.task: Assess distributor promotion commitments against expected commercial value.
reach.learn: Incremental margin, promotion funding and measurable delivery commitments.

evidence.claim: Deterministic comparisons, template generation and signature routing can reduce preparation work while people retain negotiation and approval.
The supplied digest provides no documented case establishing automated distribution negotiation or its savings.
Time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured results.

assumptions: Negotiation produces provisional terms; binding acceptance follows the approval and signature process.
Approved contract templates and commercial approval limits exist.
Template departures are flagged for legal drafting rather than generated automatically.
Access timing includes confidentiality review and employee consultation under national rules where applicable.
unknowns: Whether marketing, procurement or a commercial director leads distribution negotiations.
Which proposal fields and contract templates are standardised.
Whether the {ERP} and {OPS_SYSTEM} support compatible supplier and service identifiers.
Which commitments negotiators can make before signature.
Which access and national consultation requirements apply.
research_questions: Can source-linked extraction reliably distinguish base prices from conditional rebates and exclusions?
Which scenario calculations remain comparable across differing service commitments?
new_work: Verify extracted material terms and resolve ambiguous proposal language.
Maintain comparison rules, contract templates and approval limits.
Check that the signed version matches the approved version.
Handle connector failures and incomplete operational records.

tasks.short: Work with legal counsel to resolve copyright, licensing and royalty disputes.

steps.what: Collect disputed assets, rights agreements, correspondence and payment evidence.

loop.input: Documents from an explicitly selected case folder and permitted record exports.
loop.output: Evidence index identifying asset versions, parties, dates and missing documents.
loop.check: Retain originals and source references; verify dates and identifiers; manager checks completeness.
loop.stop: One classification pass and one correction pass; inaccessible or ambiguous items enter a missing-evidence list.
loop.why_not_simpler: Folder rules collect files, but inconsistent correspondence and asset descriptions need limited text interpretation.

steps.what: Prepare the chronology, business impact and questions for legal counsel.

loop.input: Evidence index, selected source passages and business impact notes.
loop.output: Factual chronology, disputed points and questions for counsel.
loop.check: Every factual assertion needs a source; distinguish allegations from established facts; manager checks omissions.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; unsupported statements remain explicit gaps.
loop.why_not_simpler: A fixed form captures fields, but a readable chronology requires synthesis across free-text sources.

steps.what: Assess rights, contractual obligations and legal response options.
Discuss legal options, commercial consequences and a preferred resolution.
Approve the remedy, settlement limits or escalation route.
Communicate the approved legal position to the producer or distributor.
Record resolution actions, responsible owners and deadlines.

tasks.design: Build a restricted evidence index from selected material in the {DOCS}, {EMAIL} and {ERP}; bounded loops draft a source-linked chronology and questions for counsel. Legal assessment and external responses stay with people, while the {WORKFLOW} creates actions in the {PROJECT} from structured, approved remedy fields.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence is scattered across asset versions, agreements and correspondence. Generic search retrieves documents but does not reliably establish a complete chronology.
tasks.enabler_now: Document indexing, source-linked extraction and template-based drafting can now be assembled with less coding effort. These support factual preparation without assuming improved legal reasoning.
tasks.still_hard: Rights ownership, territorial scope, disputed facts and settlement consequences require counsel. Confidentiality, privilege and access restrictions can make integration expensive.
tasks.human_edge: Counsel interprets rights and legal exposure; the manager explains business consequences and helps choose a workable remedy.
tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time reconstructing events and arrives with clearer questions for counsel. Legal advice, settlement authority and escalation rights stay unchanged.

reach.task: Identify affected published assets and coordinate approved corrections or withdrawals.
reach.learn: Asset version control, publication dependencies and rights metadata.

reach.task: Prepare a factual holding statement when a rights dispute becomes public.
reach.learn: Approved-message discipline and coordination with legal counsel.

evidence.claim: Evidence indexing and bounded factual drafting can support legal consultation without automating legal judgement.
The supplied digest provides no documented copyright or royalty dispute-resolution case supporting a stronger automation claim.
Time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured results.

assumptions: Counsel selects which case materials may be processed and where.
The tool drafts factual preparation rather than legal conclusions.
Approved remedies include structured action fields; software does not infer obligations from correspondence.
Access timing includes GDPR, confidentiality and employee consultation under national rules where applicable.
unknowns: Which materials are confidential, privileged or subject to processing restrictions.
Whether the evidence is searchable or requires document conversion.
Who can approve settlements, admissions, takedowns and royalty changes.
Which jurisdictions and national rules govern the dispute.
Whether access approval can be completed within the estimated range.
research_questions: How reliably can the evidence index distinguish asset versions and conflicting dates?
Does chronology drafting preserve disputed facts and missing evidence without implying legal conclusions?
new_work: Review evidence completeness and source links.
Maintain case access, retention settings and drafting templates.
Correct misclassified asset versions and chronology errors.
Track approved remedy actions and unresolved evidence requests.

tasks.short: Consult buying personnel about environmentally sound and sustainable product options.

steps.what: Ask buying personnel for sustainable alternatives and supporting supplier evidence.
Assemble supplier declarations, certificates and specifications for candidate products.

loop.input: Supplier declarations, certificates and specifications for explicitly selected products.
loop.output: Evidence table with product identity, stated scope, dates, source passages and gaps.
loop.check: Require source references; validate dates and identifiers; flag scope mismatches; buyer checks completeness.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass per document; unclear scope stays unresolved.
loop.why_not_simpler: Documents describe scope and qualifications inconsistently; extraction helps structure them without judging sustainability.

steps.what: Discuss product alternatives, supplier credibility, availability and environmental trade-offs.
Assess evidence limitations and environmental comparability across candidate products.
Agree which product alternatives merit further research and supplier clarification.
Record evidence gaps, research owners and follow-up deadlines.

tasks.design: Use the {WORKFLOW} to request evidence and collect selected supplier documents from the {PROCUREMENT} and {DOCS}. A bounded extraction loop builds a source-linked evidence table; people assess environmental trade-offs, and approved research actions flow into the {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supplier evidence varies in format, scope and quality. Collecting certificates is easier than determining whether products are environmentally comparable.
tasks.enabler_now: Forms, document stores and workflow rules already support collection and follow-up. AI-assisted coding and bounded extraction reduce the effort of assembling an evidence table.
tasks.still_hard: A valid certificate may cover only one facility, material or period. Environmental comparisons and marketing claims need specialist judgement and sometimes new evidence.
tasks.human_edge: Challenge supplier assertions, recognise trade-offs and distinguish substantiated improvements from attractive language.

ambition.what: Evidence-linked sustainable product shortlists for product development teams.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time chasing evidence and more time exploring credible alternatives with buying personnel. No new authority to approve environmental claims or supplier selection is assumed.

reach.task: Assess whether supplier evidence supports a proposed environmental comparison.
reach.learn: Evidence scope, functional comparability, lifecycle boundaries and uncertainty.

reach.task: Test customer needs for substantiated sustainable product alternatives.
reach.learn: Neutral question design and separating stated preference from willingness to pay.

evidence.claim: Document extraction can organise supplier evidence, but environmental validity and product comparability require specialist assessment.
The supplied digest provides no documented case establishing automated sustainable-product assessment.
Time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured results.

assumptions: Buying personnel can access supplier evidence and identify the products it covers.
A sustainability specialist or qualified external adviser is available for assessment.
Routine requests use an agreed checklist; bespoke questions remain human work.
The solution prepares research, not public environmental claims.
Access timing includes GDPR checks and employee consultation under national rules where applicable.
unknowns: Which evidence types are available and which require supplier requests.
Whether product, supplier and certificate identifiers can be matched.
Who approves environmental claims and commissions specialist assessments.
Which national rules and consultation requirements apply.
Whether a reusable checklist already exists.
research_questions: Can extraction reliably distinguish certificate holder, covered product, scope and validity period?
Which evidence gaps most often prevent useful product comparisons?
new_work: Review extracted scope and product matches.
Maintain evidence checklists and expiry reminders.
Request missing substantiation and resolve conflicting supplier statements.
Keep draft research conclusions separate from approved public claims.

role.altitude: The marketing manager gains preparation capacity across buyer consultation, distribution negotiation and legal coordination. The role remains centred on commercial judgement and relationships; formal legal, spending and publication rights do not expand automatically.
reach: Work with market research analysts to turn buyer observations into testable demand hypotheses.
Work with sustainability specialists to build evidence-linked product shortlists.
Work with editors to trace rights decisions through affected content and asset versions.
skills_to_grow: Comparing distribution economics and service trade-offs.
Checking source-linked summaries for omissions and uncertainty.
Preparing factual briefs for legal counsel.
role.ambitious_version: Run a regular category opportunity review that combines trading signals, buyer intelligence and substantiated product alternatives, then proposes focused research and distribution experiments within existing approval limits.
